subject.title: Slug alias quota (25) blocking legitimate naming migration — publisher nitishgargiitd

question: After verifying the publisher identity and affected aliases, should staff grant a one-time audited quota exception or require selected existing redirects to be released before the remaining renames proceed?
rationale: The report asks for an account-specific exception to an intentional anti-squatting control; deciding the exception scope and which redirects may be removed requires human authorization.

options.title: Grant a scoped migration exception
options.body: Authorize enough additional historical aliases for this verified publisher’s listed rename batch, with an audit record and no change to the default quota.

options.title: Release selected redirects first
options.body: Ask the publisher to identify aliases safe to retire, then free only those redirect records before continuing the renames.

options.title: Design a self-service migration policy
options.body: Pause the account action while maintainers decide whether verified batch migrations need a durable publisher-facing workflow.

recommendation.title: Grant a scoped migration exception
recommendation.body: Authorize enough additional historical aliases for this verified publisher’s listed rename batch, with an audit record and no change to the default quota.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work is the closest available history for the slug-protection and administrative-action boundary affected by this request.
